# ITEM × PHASE ENGINE — design (warm lane, for ARCHITECTURE FOR BOTH #1, #3, #4)

Principle: COMPUTE COARSE, INVALIDATE FINE; never trade warm for cold. A question exists only where an
edit can be cut off — an item in a phase. Inside one, plain fns, no bookkeeping.

## 1. What is measured today (tree 964cf5c7 = batch52 + grain)

Queries in std-avrac: 211 (164 `@query`, 31 `@cut_query`, 3+3 parted, 3 folded, 7 `@lasting`). By key
(of the 190 a signature scan classifies): item (file, at) 33 · name (file, name, …) 35 · file 43 ·
package/module 38 · other ~41 (DeclId 12, FileId 13, ImplAt, CalledFn, …).

Cold cli `tapes --findings`: 815,478 answers worked; per item ~25 law queries (21,924 items each).

Warm re-runs per edit kind, laws phase (`tapes --findings packages/cli`, one edit to
cli/src/commands/cache.av, 14 items; tool /work/meas/ip/count.py):

| edit | worked | what dominates |
|---|---|---|
| no-op | 0 | — |
| inline (module doc line) | 81 | item_under 14, item_start 14, law_findings 14 |
| literal in a body | 69 | item_under 14, item_start 14, the edited item's ~25 laws, ~12 file-level |
| comment in a body | 69 | same as literal |
| body (a statement added) | 70 | same, + typed_fn, written_typed |
| signature (a defaulted seat) | 103 | + law_findings 15, file_declares_named 8, readers' typed_fn/item_misses/receivers ×2, module_* and entry_* |
| declaration added before an item | 303 | every later item's ~25 laws again (items are keyed by POSITION), item_held 15, seats_written 12 |
| declaration added after an item | 148 | the items after it, again by position |

Three causes, in order of weight:
1. **Positional identity.** An item is (file, at). Any item added or removed renumbers every later item,
   and all of its ~25 law questions, its typing and its signature reads re-run (303 vs 70).
2. **Absolute places.** `item_start` and every finding's span are file offsets, so every item's start
   moves on any edit above it: item_under 14 + item_start 14 on every kind (28 of 69).
3. **Fine-grained law questions.** One edited item re-asks ~25 law queries plus their shared reads
   (~35 answers) where one item-phase answer would do; and a dependent reads another item's facts
   piecemeal (seats_written, written_fields, …), the decl_grain leftovers.

## 2. The query table after

| phase | question (dense key) | answer | reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| split | `items(file)` — PARTED by item id | per item: its text, kind, declared names; the file's index (name → item id) | source_text(file) |
| parse | `parse(item)` | the item's syntax, places item-relative | split part of item |
| signature | `summary(item)` | the INTERFACE: each declared name's signature, fields/variants, seats' `mut`, marks, extern/grammar/deprecation, impls it writes (target, methods, statics) — with its own hash | parse(item); summaries it names |
| types | `types(item)` | typed bodies, item-relative | parse(item); summaries of the names it uses |
| laws | `laws(item)` | every law finding of the item (laws-fusion's fold) | parse, types(item); summaries |
| lowering | `lowered(item)` | lowered bodies | types(item); summaries |
| file | `file_findings(file)`, `file_erring(file)` | the file's findings rendered, absolute places | laws parts of its items + split |
| module | `module_names(module)` — PARTED by name | declarations of a name across the module's files | split indexes of its files |
| program | walk / reached / keys (serial middle, #9) | unchanged here | lowered(item) hashes |

Survivors from today: `item_under`+`item_tape` → parse; `fn_signature`, `record_signature`,
`enum_signature`, `alias_target`, `named_shape`, `trait_method_signature`, `impl_signatures`, and my
per-name cuts (`file_declares_named`, `seats_written`, `written_fields`, `declares_extern`,
`grammar_declared`, `home_gives_named`) → PARTS of `summary(item)`; `typed_fn`, `written_typed`,
`method_body_typed` → types; `law_findings` + the ~25 `item_*` law queries → laws (laws-fusion);
`item_held`, `item_count`, `item_start`, `file_declares_at` → gone (identity is stable, places relative);
`file_declares`, `file_scope`, `module_declares` → the split index and module_names parts.
~211 queries → ~12 query kinds; everything else becomes plain fns.

## 3. Identity and keys (dense typed keys, #3)

- **Item id = (file id, declared signature key, occurrence)**, never position: a fn/type/const by its
  first declared name and kind; an impl by (target, trait); a run statement block by (kind, ordinal
  among unnamed items). Adding or removing an item renumbers nothing else.
- **A question is (phase, item id)**: two small ints. Answers live in per-phase column tables indexed by
  item id (answer hash, settled serial, value slot), so a reused ask is ONE array index plus a serial
  compare — this is engine steps 2/3/5: no argument folding, no hashed question lookup, no record box.
- Across processes the frontier keys questions by (phase, stable item key text) once per item, interned
  at load; in process everything is ints.

## 4. How reads are recorded

- Inside an item-phase: nothing is recorded; plain fns over the item's own syntax.
- At the boundary: an item-phase answer records the SUMMARY PARTS it read — (item id, name) → part
  hash — once per (reader, part), in the packed ReadTable (step 1, landed as 356be742). A read already
  recorded by this reader is skipped by a per-reader stamp on the part (step 3).
- Places inside answers are item-relative; absolute places are made only at rendering, from the
  split's item starts (not a recorded read of any later phase).

## 5. Cutoff points

1. `items(file)` part per item: an item whose text hash didn't move cuts here — its parse/summary/
   types/laws are not asked again.
2. `summary(item)`: a body, literal or comment edit leaves the summary hash standing, so no OTHER
   item re-runs (the INTERFACE FIREWALL, #4). decl_grain's leftovers (seats_written(one),
   written_fields(Box)) disappear: they are parts of a summary that didn't move.
3. `types(item)` / `laws(item)` / `lowered(item)`: each its own answer hash; file- and program-level
   gatherings re-run only over moved parts.
4. `module_names` part per name: a declaration added or renamed moves only that name's part; readers of
   other names stand.

## 6. Warm re-run counts, before → after (laws phase, same edits)

| edit | before | after (designed) | after's set |
|---|---|---|---|
| no-op | 0 | 0 | — |
| inline doc | 81 | 3 | split, parse(item 0), laws(item 0) — summary cuts |
| literal | 69 | 6 | split, parse, summary (cuts), types, laws, file_findings |
| comment | 69 | 4 | split, parse, summary (cuts), laws (types cuts on the syntax hash) |
| body | 70 | 6 | as literal |
| signature | 103 | ~10 | split, parse, summary (moves), module part, + types/laws of each reader (2 here), file_findings |
| added before an item | 303 | ~8 | split, the new item's parse/summary/types/laws, module part for its name, file_findings |
| added after an item | 148 | ~8 | as above |

The exact-count gate (doc §"warm is protected by gate") takes this table as its budget, per kind.

## 7. Order, and coordination

1. Laws first, WITH laws-fusion: their fold makes `laws(item)` one question; this lane gives it the
   stable item id and item-relative places (cause 1 and 2), measured with count.py per step.
2. `items(file)` parted + stable ids + relative places: removes item_under/item_start/item_held churn
   (−28 per edit, −~230 on an added item) — the biggest warm win and independent of the fold.
3. `summary(item)` as the one interface: the signature queries and the per-name cuts become its parts.
4. Engine: dense (phase, item) keys and column tables (steps 2/3/5 land here, not before — keying the
   old questions densely would be thrown away).
5. Types and lowering as item-phase answers.
Each step: witness (warm == cold), count.py before/after per edit kind, the cold census, the bodies-wave table.

Open questions for the lead:
- laws-fusion's fold: is its answer keyed (file, at) today? Stable ids should land under it, not beside it.
- The bodies-wave table instrumentation (parallel-main's patch) for the engine steps.

#!/bin/sh
# THE GATE, IN SLICES: every receipt a landing is held to, cut into slices that each run alone in a
# tree of their own, so N machines run N slices at once and the gate takes as long as its longest
# slice. A slice builds the compiler of HEAD itself when build/avra was built from anything else,
# runs every row on the program layer, the net off but where a row's claim is the net, empties the
# stores a cold row reads, bounds every command, keeps each row's words under build/gate/<slice>/, and
# ends with ONE line:
#   GATE <slice> <sha8> PASS|FAIL rows=<n> failed=<n> <seconds>s
# exiting 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL.
#
#   sh tools/gate.sh list               each slice, one a line, with what it holds
#   sh tools/gate.sh <slice> [arg]      one slice; the idioms slices take the base sha their diff starts at
#   sh tools/gate.sh seed               build/gate/compiler-<sha8>.tar.gz: HEAD's compiler — ONE generation, built
#                                       here first where none of HEAD's stands — and every object a tree
#                                       links with; `pack` is its other name. Run it once; every slice
#                                       then starts from `unpack` and builds nothing.
#   sh tools/gate.sh unpack <file>      seeds this tree from a pack, and holds its stamp to HEAD's: a
#                                       seeded slice builds no compiler
#
# A test row runs every suite (AVRA_SUITE_ALL=1), so it names every failing case, never only the first.
#
# GATE_OLD_PATH=0 drops every row that compares against the old path (they read AVRA_PROGRAM=0);
# when the old path goes, its default goes to 0 and those rows go with one line each.
set -u
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
cd "$root" || exit 1
unset AVRA_PROGRAM AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE
export AVRA_SUITE_ALL=1
# THE NET IS OFF unless a row's claim is the net: the old path's check before every program-layer
# compile doubles what each row costs and proves nothing a row here asks of it. The rows that keep it
# (AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1) are the ones that count what it says: the build slice's net-on cli builds and
# their "program-layer false refusal" count, the findings slices' build of every package, held to that
# same count, and the cli's suite, which holds the words a user meets through a child build/avra (at
# slice_cli). `tapes --findings` passes no door, so the net never stood in it.
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0

OLD_PATH=${GATE_OLD_PATH:-1}
# the bound of one row, and of a compiler build
ROW_SECS=${GATE_ROW_SECS:-2400}
# every `test` row's failing NAMES are held to tools/gate/<package>.names, the cases a sandbox fails
# the packages whose tests the doors slices run
DOORS_A="std-json std-task std-validate std-text std-sql std-queue std-time"

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do

logs=/work/gate-logs/$run

# the standing compiler; GATE_SEED names another (a ladder's last rung, when the tree needs one)
cp "${GATE_SEED:-$src/build/avra}" build/avra
store=$wt/build/gate-store
mkdir -p "$store"
chown -R gate:gate "$wt" "$logs"

table=$logs/table
: >"$table"
t_all=$(date +%s)
# check <name> <summary filter over the log> <command, run as gate in the worktree>
check() {
    name=$1; summ=$2; cmd=$3; log=$logs/$(echo "$name" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9_.-' '_').log
    t0=$(date +%s)
    runuser -u gate -- env HOME=/home/gate AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$store" sh -c ". /etc/profile.d/avra.sh; export AVRA_MEM_CEILING_MB=12000; cd $wt && $cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
    st=$?
    dt=$(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))
    # each `;`-part of the summary reads the whole log afresh
    s=$( (set -f; IFS=';'; for part in $summ; do sh -c "$part" <"$log" 2>/dev/null; done) | tr '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-400)
    [ -n "$s" ] || s="NO RESULT"
    if [ $st -eq 0 ]; then r=PASS; else r="FAIL(exit $st)"; fi
    printf '| %s | %s | %s | %ss |\n' "$name" "$r" "$s" "$dt" | tee -a "$table"
    return $st
}
last='grep -v "^\s*$" | tail -n 1'
findings='grep -cE "^(warning|error)\[" | sed "s/\$/ findings listed/"; grep -E "^error" | head -3'

  "$COLD make try && cp build/avra-try build/avra-oldpath"
check "P1 = new-path make try (cold)" "grep -E '^try:|held|error[:[]|Error [0-9]' | tail -3" \

check "tapes cli --built (P1)" "grep -E '^built:|^  [0-9]+ ' " "build/avra-try tapes \$PWD/packages/cli --built"
check "tapes std-avrac --ran" "grep -E '^ran:' | cut -c1-260" "build/avra-try tapes \$PWD/packages/std-avrac --ran"
check "tapes std-relation --ran" "grep -E '^ran:'" "build/avra-try tapes \$PWD/packages/std-relation --ran"

check "runtime-tests each (-D_GNU_SOURCE, diagnostic)" "grep -E '^(RT|rt-)' | tail -40" '
  make -s build/std_io.o >/dev/null

    then p=$((p+1)); else f=$((f+1)); bad="$bad $n"; fi; done
  echo "RT $p passed, $f failed:${bad:- none} (of $(ls runtime/tests/*.c | wc -l))"; [ $f -eq 0 ]'

  "AVRA_PROGRAM=0 build/avra-try check packages/std-program --baseline tools/idioms.baseline"
# a leak frees nothing twice, so the RC guard cannot see one; the soundness checker does

  "AVRA_PROGRAM=0 AVRA_SOUND_CHECK=1 build/avra-try check packages/cli >build/sound.out 2>&1; s=\$?; cat build/sound.out; ! grep -q 'defect: in \`' build/sound.out && exit \$s"
for w in tools/witness_program_*.sh; do
    check "$(basename "$w" .sh)" "$last" "sh $w"

# only), so each --rc case is wrapped as its own package under build/rc-pkgs/ for the program-layer

rcpkg() { # rcpkg <dir> <source .av> [<.expected>]: a package whose bin is the file
    mkdir -p "$1/src"; cp "$2" "$1/src/main.av"; [ -z "${3:-}" ] || [ ! -f "$3" ] || cp "$3" "$1/main.expected"
    printf '[package]\nname        = "%s"\nversion     = "0.0.1"\ndescription = "a gate case, wrapped"\n\n[bin]\nname = "%s"\npath = "src/main.av"\n' \
      "$(basename "$1")" "$(basename "$1")" >"$1/avra.toml"
}
# the build through the program layer, proven by its own words; the product is <pkg>/src/main
PLB='AVRA_PROGRAM=1 AVRA_QUERY_TIMES=1 build/avra-try build $pkg >build/rc.plb.out 2>&1 || { grep -v "^time:\|^phases:\|^ahead\|^split:" build/rc.plb.out | tail -3; exit 2; }; grep -q "asking the program layer" build/rc.plb.out || { echo "VOID: the build did not go through the program layer"; exit 3; }'
control_ok=0
if [ -n "$rcs" ]; then
    find build/rc-pkgs -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null; mkdir -p build/rc-pkgs/rc_control
    cat >build/rc-pkgs/control.av <<'CONTROL'

fi
	@$(MAKE) -s ready

# THE TREE A PROGRAM BUILDS IN: every package's C object, which a native
# link names, and the wasm runtime with the wasm package objects, which a
# page's build names. Without a wasm toolchain here the second half is
# skipped, spoken — a page build then refuses by name.
ready: $(PACKAGE_OBJS)
	@if $(WASM_CC) --target=$(WASM_TARGET) -print-file-name=crt1.o 2>/dev/null | grep -q /; then \
	    $(MAKE) -s wasm-runtime wasm-packages || exit 1; \
	else \
	    echo "ready: no WASI libc for $(WASM_CC) — a page build needs one (README.md); native programs are ready"; \
	fi

# A REFUSAL MUST SPEAK: the build's own words went to /dev/null, so a compiler
# that refused its own source reported only "make: *** Error 2" and the next
# reader ran `./avra build packages/cli` by hand to find out why.
avra: $(COMPILER_OBJS)
	@mkdir -p build
	@# the log is BOUNDED: only its last 200 KB is ever read, and a build failing in a
	@# loop filled the volume twice (tools/capped.sh, which also carries the status).
	@sh tools/capped.sh build/avra-build.out 200000 ./avra build packages/cli || { cat build/avra-build.out; exit 1; }
	@mkdir -p build
	@cp packages/cli/src/main build/avra
	@codesign -f -s - build/avra 2>/dev/null || true
	@rm -f packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll
	@# what this binary was built from, for a worktree that wants to start from it
	@sh tools/work built-from . > build/.avra-built-from 2>/dev/null || rm -f build/.avra-built-from
	@sh tools/work deposit . || true
	@echo "avra: build/avra"

# WHAT A COMPILER BUILD LEAVES, one path a line: the binary, its hot leaves
# and every object it links with each object's stamp and dependency list.
# A cache of built compilers (tools/sprite-remote.sh) keeps exactly these.
compiler-files:
	@printf '%s\n' build/avra build/avra_hot.bc build/avra_hot.inc $(sort $(COMPILER_OBJS) \
	  $(patsubst %.o,%.sha,$(filter %.o,$(COMPILER_OBJS))) $(patsubst %.o,%.d,$(filter %.o,$(COMPILER_OBJS))))

# THE COMPILER FROM WHATEVER STANDS: the standing binary builds this tree
# GENS times (one `make avra` advances one generation; two reach a fixed point), and where none stands or
# it cannot read the tree — new syntax, a refusal about its own source — the
# seed bootstraps it, a FULL build, so a source wrong for real still dies.
# A SEED EMITTED FROM THIS VERY SOURCE comes first: linking it already is the
# compiler this tree builds (tools/seed_is_tree.sh), so no ladder and no
# standing compiler can do better, and a tree too new for every published one
# still builds; with rungs named, it is their product too.
# RUNGS are the tree's `Rung:` commits, oldest first (tools/rungs.sh): each is
# built by the product of the one before (tools/ladder.sh), starting from the
# standing compiler or the seed as linked, and HEAD by the last; a laddered
# tree never falls back to the seed, which cannot read a rung. The last rung's
# product stays at build/avra-ladder. LADDER_BASE is the base each rung is
# replayed on (tools/ladder.sh's AVRA_LADDER_BASE). GEN_BOUND bounds each build in seconds
# (tools/bounded.sh names the cause), LADDER_BOUND the whole ladder; STORE_ASIDE
# is where an older compiler's store goes before the bootstrap, since a store is
# one compiler's.
RUNGS ?=
LADDER_BASE ?=
GEN_BOUND ?=
LADDER_BOUND ?= 900
STORE_ASIDE ?=
GENS ?= 2
BOUNDED = $(if $(GEN_BOUND),sh tools/bounded.sh $(GEN_BOUND) )
compiler:
	@gens() { n=$(GENS); while [ "$$n" -gt 0 ]; do $(BOUNDED)$(MAKE) -s avra || return 1; n=$$((n - 1)); done; }; \
	if [ "$$(sh tools/seed_is_tree.sh "$$(sh tools/sources_hash.sh)" "$$(cat bootstrap/seed.sources 2>/dev/null)")" = seed ]; then \
	  echo "compiler: the committed seed was emitted from this tree — linked, not climbed"; \
	  $(BOUNDED)$(MAKE) -s bootstrap || exit 1; \
	  [ -z "$(strip $(RUNGS))" ] || cp build/avra build/avra-ladder; \
	elif [ -n "$(strip $(RUNGS))" ]; then \
	  [ -x build/avra ] || $(MAKE) -s recover || { echo "compiler: the ladder has no start — none stands and the seed did not link"; exit 1; }; \
	  product=$$(AVRA_LADDER_BASE=$(LADDER_BASE) AVRA_LADDER_S=$(LADDER_BOUND) sh tools/ladder.sh build/avra $(RUNGS)) \
	    || { echo "compiler: the ladder failed — a rung did not build with the compiler of the rung before it"; exit 1; }; \
	  cp "$$product" build/avra-ladder && cp "$$product" build/avra; \
	  sh tools/ladder.sh --clean "$${AVRA_LADDER_DIR:-$${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/ladder}"; \
	  gens || { echo "compiler: the ladder's product did not build this tree — no seed can read a rung"; exit 1; }; \
	elif [ -x build/avra ] && gens; then :; else \
	  if [ -n "$(STORE_ASIDE)" ] && [ -d .avra-cache ]; then mv .avra-cache "$(STORE_ASIDE)"; fi; \
	  echo "compiler: the standing compiler did not build this tree — bootstrapping from the seed"; \
	  $(BOUNDED)$(MAKE) -s bootstrap; \
	fi

# THE EDIT LOOP: the source built by the STANDING compiler into
# build/avra-try, never over it — so the builder's print, and every row its
# store holds, stands from one edit to the next. `./avra-try` runs it. A
# change the compiler must READ to build itself (codegen, the front end, a
# refusal about its own source) reaches the product only through `make avra`.
try: $(COMPILER_OBJS)
	@sh tools/capped.sh build/avra-try-build.out 200000 ./avra build packages/cli --time || { cat build/avra-try-build.out; exit 1; }
	@grep '^time: ast' build/avra-try-build.out | grep -oE 'held [0-9]+/[0-9]+' || true
	@cp packages/cli/src/main build/avra-try
	@codesign -f -s - build/avra-try 2>/dev/null || true
	@rm -f packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll
	@echo "try: build/avra-try — ./avra-try runs it"

# THE WARM EDIT LOOP, measured: a one-edit check and build of the cli, and `make try` on a leaf and a core edit.
edit-loop:
	@sh tools/db_measure/edit_loop.sh

# THE INSTALL: the binary under bin/, and what it finds from its own
# directory — the runtime's object and every std package — under
# lib/avra/. A program anywhere then says `use @std.io` with no
# manifest row, and links.
PREFIX ?= /usr/local
install: avra
	@mkdir -p $(PREFIX)/bin $(PREFIX)/lib/avra/std
	@cp build/avra $(PREFIX)/bin/avra
	@cp $(RUNTIME_LIB) $(PREFIX)/lib/avra/libavra_runtime.a
	@for p in packages/std-*; do rm -rf $(PREFIX)/lib/avra/std/$$(basename $$p); cp -R $$p $(PREFIX)/lib/avra/std/; done
	@rm -rf $(PREFIX)/lib/avra/dom && cp -R runtime/dom $(PREFIX)/lib/avra/dom
	@echo "install: $(PREFIX)/bin/avra, $$(ls -d packages/std-* | wc -l | tr -d ' ') std packages under $(PREFIX)/lib/avra/std"

content.content:
# HANDOFF — warm lane ("fold" / engine lane), 2026-11-19

## Lane and scope
The warm-edit lane for the Lead (controller over the claude-bridge). Goal: cheap, correct warm edits
of packages/cli; the ITEM × PHASE ENGINE design of record (`meas/ITEM_PHASE_DESIGN.md`, filed in the
lead's ARCHITECTURE_FOR_BOTH as #1/#3/#4); engine cost work (packed reads, dense keys).
Ownership: program_code_hashes and start-up are parallel-main's; pack search/index is parallel-main's;
laws fold is laws-fusion's; exact-count gate (tools/cost.sh, cost_ratchet.py) is wrong-answers'.

## Base
`batch54` = 99def0d2 (bundle /work/batch54.bundle, prereq d750dfa7). Branch `engine-54` in the
worktree /work/wt-t, head **846ae956**. Bundles here:
- `lane.bundle` = engine-54 ^d750dfa70 (everything)
- `lane-since-batch54.bundle` = engine-54 ^batch54 (the 12 commits below)
- `uncommitted.patch` is empty: nothing uncommitted.

## Commits ahead of batch54 (oldest first)
- 9c76559e names: per-name/per-item cut queries over a file's declarations (file_declares_named/_at,
  item_held, written_fields, seats_written, declares_extern, grammar_declared, home_gives_named; resolved cuts)
- 06969a2e decl_grain spec: an edit's own-cost queries named per case, each once and cut (12/13 pass)
- 53e458de Merge batch52 (per-name reads over resolve-2's marks/problems/members)
- 964cf5c7 Merge batch52 d7102ad5 (sugars fix)
- 72e18dd1 engine: packed ReadTable (reads as columns; census cold tapes --findings 725.3M -> 704.9M boxes)
- ebdc15c5 step 2a: a file's items as parts (item_parts: text part and start part per item)
- f416b51f step 2a: item_front / item_said per item (ran_before, use_faults, first_running, worn_in_item)
- 2828a6d1 step 2a: laws read per-name answers (contexts_declared, records_with_field, method_owners)
  and the entry only where the item runs (runs_in guard)
- e07c0e04 read table idioms (pushes unrolled)
- 2e0fb566 Merge batch53 (holds_manifest kept)
- df52f711 Merge batch54 (item_uses: batch54's `lines.is_empty()` early return + item_front reads)
- 846ae956 step 2c: earlier use lines reach later items without places; item_start a plain part read

engine-54 up to df52f711 was SENT as /work/engine-54.bundle (for batch 54). 846ae956 is NOT sent yet.

## In flight when stopped
- Proofs of 846ae956: avrac-a, -g, program, -f, -b, -c PASS; idioms std-avrac rc=0; cold time
  82.2 -> 78.5 user-s (no regression). avrac-d/-e were running; edit witness NOT run yet on 846ae956.
- cli slice FAILS on `avra db diff` (db_diff_test.av): it fails identically on batch54 ALONE (0/7),
  so it's batch54's/environment's, unpinned. Report it with the 846ae956 bundle.
- witness section `derived` fails on batch53 and batch54 ALONE (parity-values' fix not yet landed).

Warm re-runs (count.py, parent-only, cache.av; laws phase), before step 2 -> now:
noop 0, inline 81->43, literal 69->39, comment 69->39, body 70->40, signature 103->65,
added-before 303->266, added-after 148->70. Each edit's own-item laws re-run: 1 (signature 2).
NOTE: the gate counts ALL processes with work-ahead off (Lead's numbers: signature 172, added-before
418, added-after 244 before). Re-base the design budgets on tools/cost.sh once it lands (batch 54).

## Next 3, in order
1. Finish proofs of 846ae956 (avrac-d/e, full edit witness minus `derived`), bundle batch54..HEAD.
2. Step 2b: STABLE ITEM IDS under laws-fusion's fold (their bundle 7, keyed (file, at)): replace `at`
   with the item id inside the fold's key (Lead: never a parallel key). Positional sites: 34 loops over
   0..item_count, 105 item_held guards, 5 "items before at" readers (now item_front/item_said),
   generated-item numbering (generated_at: at - item_count). Target: added-before 266 -> ~8.
3. summary(item) as the interface firewall (design §2/§5), then engine dense (phase, item) keys
   (engine steps 2/3/5: one-probe reused ask, skip known reads, settled answers as columns).

## Open asks / rulings
- tools/cost.sh exact invocation (ask the Lead until batch 54 lands).
- parity-values' fix for the `derived` witness section.
- bodies-wave instrumentation: /work/lead/bodies-wave/ (README, measure.patch, families.py, bwsplit3.py).
- Engine plan approved: steps 2, 3, 5 GO; #4 (no decode) measure first (~1 s); #6 only the claim skip.

## Trip wires for a fresh session
- Build a tree: `AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make avra` (builder = build/avra of the same lineage). batch52+ needs a
  batch-52-lineage builder; the committed seed is too old (don't `make bootstrap`). Kept binaries in
  /work/wt-t/build: avra-964 (batch52 merge), avra-53, avra-54 (df52f711), avra-2c (846ae956),
  avra-trace (why-trace build). /work/avra/build/avra-b53, avra-b54 = batch53/54 alone.
- `make avra` rewrites the tracked packages/cli/src/.main.print — `git checkout -- packages/cli/src/.main.print`.
- Names are flat across a package's modules AND clash across packages in derived code (ItemPlace in
  std-program broke a build with only "a seat refuses a value here"; `AVRA_PROGRAM=0 build/avra check`
  names such clashes).
- My per-name rewrite (regex in meas/ notes) re-applied after merges turns item_held's and
  file_declares_named's own definitions into self-calls: fix them back every time.
- Measurement: `python3 meas/count.py <compiler> <tag> <tree>` (tapes --findings, cache.av edits).
  Why-trace: apply meas/why-trace.patch to std-program query_engine.av, build, run with
  AVRA_WHY_TRACE=1 (each re-run's moved reads) or AVRA_STOP_READ/_READ2/_ASKER/_ASKER2 +
  AVRA_STOP_REPLAY=1 + AVRA_TRAP_TRACE=1 (backtrace at a named read). Never commit that patch.
- Census: `CENSUS_CAP_MB=12000 sh tools/census.sh tapes --findings packages/cli` (4 GB cap kills it).
- Edit witness: meas/proofH.sh (runs in /work/wt-t with build/avra-e3; clear .avra-cache first;
  ~1.6 h; split slices and witness into separate jobs: background job limit 2 h).
- Disk fills: clear /work/avra/build/scratch and old build/avra-* with find -delete.
- Rules: commit as you go, push nowhere, no rm/stash/reset --hard, fmt touched .av, hand back via
  git bundle + bridge send_files + a ≤12-line post.

#!/bin/sh
# THE PRE-GATE, on worktree /work/gate-wt of /work/avra. Two steps:
#   sh /work/gate.sh merge <base> [ref|file.bundle:branch]...
#       checks out <base> (a ref, or file.bundle:branch), merges the rest in order;
#       a conflict lists its files and stops (the tree is left mid-merge for a decision).
#   sh /work/gate.sh check [--rc FILE]... [--test FILE]...
#       the full gate on the worktree's HEAD, one heavy job at a time, every build cold,
#       every check as non-root user `gate`; GATE_SEED=<compiler> overrides the standing $src/build/avra. --rc runs AVRA_RC_GUARD=1 over a lone program
#       file (evaluator, native old path, native program layer; output vs its .expected);
#       --test runs `avra test FILE`. Each --rc case is also wrapped as a package for its
#       program-layer row, after a positive control that must abort under the guard. Every tools/witness_program_*.sh is run.
# Prints one table (check | result | detail | wall). Logs in /work/gate-logs/<run>/.
set -u
src=/work/avra
wt=/work/gate-wt
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
export AVRA_MEM_CEILING_MB=12000

resolve() { # a ref, or file.bundle:branch fetched into refs/gate/<file>/<branch>
    case $1 in
        *.bundle:*)
            f=${1%%:*}; b=${1#*:}; [ -f "$f" ] || f=/work/$f
            n=$(basename "$f" .bundle)
            git -C "$src" fetch -q "$f" "+refs/heads/*:refs/gate/$n/*" || return 1
            echo "refs/gate/$n/$b" ;;
        *) echo "$1" ;;
    esac
}

if [ "${1:-}" = merge ]; then
    shift
    find "$src/.git" -name '._*' -delete 2>/dev/null
    [ -e "$wt/.git" ] || git -C "$src" worktree add -f --detach "$wt" program >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "gate: worktree add failed"; exit 2; }
    cd "$wt" || exit 2
    git merge --abort 2>/dev/null
    base=$(resolve "$1") || exit 3; shift
    git checkout -q -f --detach "$base" || { echo "gate: checkout $base failed"; exit 2; }
    git clean -q -f -d -e build/ >/dev/null
    echo "base $base = $(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD)"
    for m in "$@"; do
        r=$(resolve "$m") || exit 3
        if git -c user.name=gate -c user.email=gate@localhost merge -q --no-ff --no-edit "$r" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "merged $m ($(git rev-parse --short=8 "$r")) -> $(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD)"
        else
            echo "MERGE CONFLICT merging $m ($(git rev-parse --short=8 "$r")) onto $(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD):"
            git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | sed 's/^/  /'
            exit 4
        fi
    done
    exit 0

1	# Avra — clean-room compiler
2	
3	## AVRA PRINCIPLES
4	
5	The spec's Part 0 frames every decision (full text: spec, Part 0).
6	Above all: **P6, paradox collapse** — binary choices are usually false
7	dichotomies; find the design where both sides win. When a trade-off
8	feels forced, the model is wrong, not the requirements.
9	
10	- P1  LLM-first: correct on first generation is the success metric
11	- P2  substrate for autonomous services
12	- P3  gloriously declarative, zero ceremony
13	- P4  Rust-level performance or better
14	- P5  full-stack vertical integration
15	- P6  paradox collapse
16	- P7  visible magic — always inspectable
17	- P8  escape hatches everywhere
18	- P9  boundaries are contracts
19	- P10 the compiler holds semantic knowledge no other tool has
20	- P11 machine-readability is the substrate, human-readability the projection
21	- P12 one source of truth, many projections
22	- P13 collapse dev/ops/infra
23	- P14 no runtime, no framework, no container
24	- P17 composability over featurefulness
25	
26	Clean restart of the Avra compiler, built slowly, one reviewed file at a
27	time. Front end first: an extensible grammar assembled from
28	LanguageFeature components, producing an AST for later passes.
29	Toolchain: the compiler builds itself — `./avra` runs `build/avra`,
30	and a cold tree bootstraps from `bootstrap/seed.ll.gz` (`make bootstrap`;
31	README.md).
32	
33	Design sources of truth (in `../forge-crafting-intepreters`):
34	- `docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md` — the language
35	- `docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md` — node model, spans, error tolerance
36	- `bootstrap/docs/2026_08_19_STANDARDIZATION.md` — front-end shape
37	
38	Follow the old tree's *documented designs*, never its code habits.
39	
40	## Comments
41	
42	Never write comments about specific situations, tickets, approaches, or
43	points in time. Comments are evergreen: always relevant, or absent.
44	Keep them very terse, in plain language. State what a thing is or the
45	invariant it holds — no narration, no self-justification, no history.
46	
47	## The idiom bar — BEFORE writing any fn
48	
49	First drafts are written idiomatic, not cleaned up later. Before
50	the body exists, answer:
51	
52	1. Is any loop a MAP/FILTER/FLAT-MAP? Comprehension (`?` works in
53	   element and iterable; predicates hoist into named fns).
54	2. Building head-plus-tail? `concat` (a list METHOD) / `flatten`
55	   (core's FREE fn — `flatten(xs)`, never `xs.flatten()`), never
56	   push-ceremony.
57	3. Is a projection being spelled twice? The second spelling names a
58	   verb (`cx.int_at`, `expr_fps`) or uses the existing one.
59	4. Does absence read straight? (`?? `, `?.`, if-null early return —
60	   never a two-arm null match without payload logic on both arms.)
61	5. Scanning for one element? `find`/`any`/`index_of`, not a flag
62	   loop.
63	6. Unsure a shape compiles in the subset? PROBE in scratch first —
64	   fear of traps is how ugly-but-safe drafts happen, and every
65	   probe result gets recorded so the fear shrinks.
66	
67	DOGFOODING.md is the full rulebook; `avra check --baseline
68	tools/idioms.baseline` FAILS on any NEW site — the baseline lists
69	sites, never counts, and no tool path can add to it (`make idioms`
70	runs every package, `make idioms-accept` prunes what a fix made
71	gone). Every idiom the language can state is a `rule` declaration,
72	found by `avra check` itself, and the gate counts a RULE's finding
73	only — `type.alias_copy` wears the same `warning[kind]` shape and is
74	the compiler's own law, never a rule, so the gate reads the rule
75	table (`avra rules --json`), never a kind-string shape. Accepted
76	debt lives in the baseline alone, reviewed at adoption and every
77	time after. A new idiom lands in DOGFOODING's registry AT DISCOVERY,
78	named by its rule — `<module>.<rule>`, never a number.
79	
80	## Style
81	
82	- Inline single-use values. A `let` earns its place only when the
83	  name carries meaning the expression lacks, the value is read more
84	  than once, or the subset REQUIRES a pin (a `dyn` value selected
85	  among arms, a Result-answering lambda — "The subset today" names
86	  each). Empty literals (`[]`, `{}`) infer inline in
87	  constructor fields — never bind them to a throwaway name. When a
88	  pin seems needed, probe before assuming.
89	- A state struct's impl is its VOCABULARY: the small verbs that
90	  read or write its tables (`speak`, `bind`, `mint`, `give`) live
91	  as methods, so drivers read as prose. The free state fns the
92	  bootstrap habit left (`eval_node(ev, cx, e)`, the interpreter's
93	  `put(m, …)`, the backend's `define(em, …)`) are methods now, and
94	  so are the pass contexts' whole vocabularies (`cx.accepts(e,
95	  want)`, `cx.open_region(c)`, `ws.sig(d)` — 320 verbs, one sweep);
96	  style.free_state_verb refuses a new free verb in the pass's own files. A PASS ENTRY
97	  POINT (`lower(a: Analysis)`, `memory(l: Lowered)`) keeps the one
98	  standard signature and is not a verb.
99	- A long fn splits at its PHASE boundaries into named helpers, each
100	  with a one-line contract (`match_seq` matches, `built` builds —
101	  grammar/executor.av; `window` frames, `severity_word` branches —
102	  diagnostics/render.av). If a fn needs a paragraph comment
103	  mid-body, that paragraph is a helper's name.
104	- A LAW never assembles PROSE: every refusal is a NAMED VOICE fn
105	  (its whole body the one `spoken`/`emit`), in a voices section at
106	  the file's tail or shared where features share words. Rule
107	  bodies read as guard + verb (rule.compiler.refusal_assembled;
108	  enums/check.av is the exemplar).
109	  AND A VOICE STATES THE LAW, NOT THE SYMPTOM. "a pointer's only
110	  constant is null" is the rule; "both engines read it as null" was
111	  the observation that happened to hold the day it was written. A
112	  symptom-worded refusal goes STALE the moment the mechanism moves,
113	  and until then it reads as a workaround for a quirk rather than a
114	  rule to obey — so it teaches the reader to look for the quirk. The
115	  law's wording outlives its own implementation, which is what makes
116	  it worth pinning in the golden (lower.av's pointer-constant guard).
117	- A BUILDER'S WORDS ARE ITS CLAIM. A builder's refusal is carried
118	  WHOLE into its diagnostic (grammar/executor.av's build phase:
119	  `cause: Cause.Builder, message: m`), so a message that is a LAW
120	  the writer broke reads as the law, and one that is a DEFECT says
121	  so in its own words. A blanket "builder failed:" prefix once told
122	  the reader the compiler had broken about every law — five of the
123	  seven refusals sampled at c7b5038 — while `Cause` had separated
124	  `Builder` from `Defect` all along: the seam was right and only the
125	  WORDING lied. THE GENERAL SHAPE: A PARAPHRASE OF A FLAG IS A
126	  SECOND COPY, and the reader believes the words — the flag is
127	  checked by the code, the prose by nobody. So the WORDS carry the
128	  CLAIM and the STRUCTURE carries the CATEGORY (`Cause.Builder`
129	  projects to F0102, compiler/codes.av), and the words never restate
130	  the category.
131	- A projection is ONE match: nested patterns
132	  (`.Node(.NAlt(a)) -> a, _ -> null`), never an unwrap ladder.
133	- The third copy of a shape names the concept: shared walks and
134	  registries get ONE definition (`post_order`, `file_command`) and
135	  the copies die. Two copies may wait; three never do.
136	
137	## Dogfooding is design
138	
139	The compiler is Avra's first user. When its code WANTS a construct
140	the language lacks — a sugar, a projection, a rule — add the ask to
141	the ROADMAP's sugar backlog, naming the wanting site, as part of the
142	change that hit it. Request your own features: the backlog feeds the
143	spec. The same discipline runs one level down: a PATTERN discovered
144	while writing (a beautiful form, a smell, a licensed exception) is
145	an IDIOM — it lands in DOGFOODING.md's registry at discovery, and
146	the greppable ones become `rule` declarations `avra check` finds
147	directly (compiler/idioms.av, or a feature's own idioms.av). The
148	registry is the idiom engine's spec, written by dogfooding.
149	
150	## Rules
151	
152	- `core/` is infrastructure only. Features never import features.
153	- Layering is one-way: core -> grammar -> features -> compiler, all
154	  over `@std/relation`, whose `engine/` is the memo kernel —
155	  infrastructure, language-agnostic, the one a running program asks too.
156	  `grammar/` is the language-agnostic engine; `compiler/` is the
157	  driver and the ONE definition of Avra (feature order is branch
158	  order is the language).
159	- No string tags or string-matching to detect behavior.
160	- `_ ->` over our own enums is decided by COUNTING THE ANSWERING
161	  ARMS. One arm answers -> a PROJECTION, and the catch-all is
162	  honest: its contract pins the answer for variants that do not
163	  exist yet. TWO OR MORE answer -> a REGISTRY, and a catch-all there
164	  silently forgets the next variant (`let_name` dropped For's
165	  counter exactly so; `type_decl_name` would have swallowed the next
166	  type-declaring statement). Registries spell every arm — `or`-runs
167	  keep that affordable. Ratcheted as style.registry_catchall AND held by the compiler:
168	  F2040 counts the ANSWERING ARMS over the declared enum and names
169	  the variants a hole would forget. The license is a SPELLING, not a
170	  comment — `rest ->` says the remainder is deliberate, and both the
171	  compiler and the ratchet read it. The two licensed shapes are a
172	  feature matching its own variants (it cannot enumerate other
173	  features') and a loop that DELEGATES the rest to an exhaustive
174	  dispatch — each writes `rest ->` at the site.
175	  AND THE LAW IS ABOUT THE TEST, NOT THE MATCH. For a REGISTRY enum
176	  `is .Variant` IS A CATCH-ALL IN DIFFERENT CLOTHES: a boolean that
177	  asks about ONE variant and falls through for the rest discharges
178	  the registry's obligation no better than `_ ->`, and it is harder
179	  to see. For a PROJECTION enum it stays the right idiom. Two
180	  `RtKind` consumers were written that way (`rt_arg`, `answers_word`
181	  in llvm.av), correct only while the enum had three variants —
182	  widening it to carry C's integer widths would have sent an Avra
183	  `int` into an `i32` seat with no truncation, compiling clean. Both
184	  are exhaustive matches now.
185	  ENFORCEMENT SPLITS FROM THE LAW HERE, deliberately: no grep tells a
186	  registry enum from a projection one, so this gets NO ratchet rule.
187	  The keeper is `make vocab`, a CURATED table naming each registry's
188	  consumers and refusing BOTH shapes inside them — the table says
189	  which registries it holds, and a registry it does not name is
190	  unguarded. Naming the next one IS how this law is enforced.
191	  AND THE OBLIGATION CROSSES INTO C, where no keeper can follow. The
192	  runtime's `acc_kind_of` was a kind-keyed ternary falling through to
193	  ACC_RECORD — correct for the three kinds that existed when it was
194	  written and wrong from that same day for `KIND_STATIC`, so every
195	  immortal string was filed as a RECORD by `AVRA_MEM_STATS`: the
196	  instrument THIS FILE names as the way to answer a memory question,
197	  miscounting its own data since birth. A C chain keyed on our kinds
198	  carries a registry's obligation and `make vocab` cannot see it, so
199	  spell the kinds there too.
200	  AND THE REASON IT HID GENERALIZES: `RtKind` had three variants from
201	  the day it was written and had not yet grown — it carries six now
202	  — so nothing ever tested the assumption. A KEEPER THAT HAS ONLY
203	  EVER GUARDED A STATIC ENUM IS UNTESTED — the first widening is its
204	  first real test, and that is the worst moment to learn it was only
205	  ever looking for one shape.
206	  AND THE OBLIGATION CROSSES A PACKAGE BOUNDARY TOO, not only into C.
207	  A registry keyed on ANOTHER PACKAGE'S enum is spelled over NAMES —
208	  `node_value` matches `@std.meta.Node`'s variant names, because a
209	  foreign enum has no typed id here — so no compiler law and no grep
210	  sees it, and its `_ -> null` forgot the next variant the way every
211	  registry hole does: a template generated nothing and nobody was
212	  told. The keeper cannot follow across the seam; spell the arms and
213	  make the unknown SPEAK.
214	- THE EXEMPTION LAW, which the above is one instance of: a doctrine
215	  exemption that is not written AT THE SITE is an unbounded amnesty.
216	  Prose exemptions are invisible to tooling and to the next reader,
217	  so they rot into the default. Every licensed deviation carries
218	  `// LICENSED I<n>: <reason>` where the code is — that is what
219	  makes `make idioms` able to demand a decision instead of guessing
220	  which deviations were once approved.
221	- Node facts (spans included) live in side tables keyed by typed ids,
222	  never on nodes.
223	- A SLOT'S SEED IS COMPUTED THE SAME WAY AS ITS UPDATES, or the
224	  first decision judges a different quantity from every later one —
225	  and only the first, which is what makes it invisible.
226	  `collapse_breaks` seeded `line_indent` from `raw[0].span.lo`, a
227	  byte OFFSET, and assigned it a character DISTANCE everywhere after;
228	  the seed read as a column only while the first token sat on line
229	  one, so a LEADING COMMENT's own length became the indent and a
230	  four-character comment changed how the file parsed. Write the seed
231	  as the update's rule applied to nothing, not as whatever value
232	  happens to be at hand.
233	- A fact EVERY BODY MAY READ is answered from the PROGRAM — the
234	  store — never from a pass's fact tables. Fact tables are per
235	  declaration, over that declaration's expression range alone, so an
236	  answer computed from `facts` is right in the body that recorded it
237	  and WRONG everywhere else (a const's declared `int?` read back as
238	  `int` across a fn floor, and `??` warned it would never fire).
239	  The store holds what the program wrote; that is what shared
240	  answers are made of.
241	- A law that HOLDS A BINDING TO ITS ANNOTATION compares the value to
242	  the DECLARED type it computed, never to the binding's own type —
243	  asking the binding for its type compares the value against itself,
244	  and the law silently stops refusing anything.
245	- Ask a BINDING, never a NAME, whether it is a const/a capture/a
246	  seat. A name may be defined twice (a `let` shadowing a const), so
247	  a name-keyed question and the binding in hand answer about
248	  DIFFERENT statements — the mismatch reads a slot nobody wrote
249	  ("index -1"). One question, asked of the statement. And a
250	  name-keyed table holds what it holds: `resolve_assign` asked
251	  `binding_of(name)`, a LOCALS table, so a fn's name walked
252	  through as a place — the walk had already recorded the root's
253	  binding; ask that.
254	- A BODY IS TYPED UNDER ITS SIGNATURE, so a declaration whose
255	  SIGNATURE WAS REFUSED has no scope for its body to be typed in —
256	  and the empty list that stands in for the missing one is read as
257	  a real scope by every seat. `walk_under` sets `self.scope =
258	  sig?.params ?? []`, the plausible default the protocol law
259	  refuses, and `target_type`'s `.Param(i) -> self.scope[i]` then
260	  indexed past the end: a generic METHOD is refused whole (F2031,
261	  no sig recorded) and its body still walks, so `fn f<T: Tr>(x: T)
262	  { x.m() }` inside an `impl` CRASHED THE COMPILER while the same
263	  fn at the top level was fine. The tell was a SIBLING PAIR
264	  disagreeing in one match — `.Receiver -> self.scope.first() ??
265	  self.error_type` was total and `.Param(i)` was not, four lines
266	  apart, so one seat kind had the guard and the other did not.
267	  SEVERAL SPELLINGS OF ONE QUESTION IS THE DEFECT, not the missing
268	  bound: every one asks "what type does seat i wear", and one file
269	  held five — two receiver reads, total, and three parameter reads,
270	  none of them. The split was invisible because each pair sat
271	  inside ONE match, arms apart, so a reader checking either arm saw
272	  a guard right beside it. There is one reader now (`seat_type`),
273	  and the refusal was already spoken before the body ran, which is
274	  what makes Error the honest answer rather than a defect voice.
275	- A COPIED TEMPLATE'S SPANS ARE ITS ORIGIN FILE'S OFFSETS — so its
276	  errors point home — and any pass that reads a span as THIS file's
277	  offset must ask `store.spanned_elsewhere(e)` first. `range_bodies`
278	  did not, and `within`'s copied nodes landed in whatever `client.av`
279	  declared at `time.av`'s offsets (a write through `self` blamed on
280	  `describe`). A sublanguage's nodes are foreign too but spanned HERE
281	  (shifted into the block); `ForeignRange.spanned_home` tells them apart.
282	- A READ WEARS THE TYPE OF WHAT IS READ, never the type of the node
283	  doing the reading. This bit THREE times in one slice: a captured
284	  callee took the CALL's type (a call's type is its answer, never its
285	  callee's), a capture took the LAMBDA's type (a lambda is a managed
286	  box, so an `int` capture looked managed and the memory pass
287	  retained a number), and a field read took the field expression's
288	  type where the SUBJECT's decides the layout. A register's recorded
289	  type is the wrong witness under mono, where it may still name a
290	  type parameter; the STATIC type of the thing being read is right.
291	- UNIFY BINDS, `accepts` RECORDS. `unify` agrees two types and pins a
292	  declaration's Vars; it does NOT record the lift that lowering
293	  mints. A seat that unifies and returns without passing through the
294	  agreement door silently drops the widen — invisible for as long as
295	  the widen happens to be identity, and a wrong answer the day the
296	  representation changes. The door is ONE verb, `agreed` (checks.av),
297	  and the three unified seats — a call argument, a struct field, an
298	  enum payload — call it; the payload once short-circuited and
299	  refused a `dyn` box and an auto-Ok its siblings took
300	  (compiler/tests/seats holds the proof).
301	- EVERY POINTER AVRA HOLDS CARRIES A HEADER. The runtime counts
302	  references in sixteen bytes BEFORE each payload (tag, kind, rc,

671	  SEQUENCES HAS A BOUNDARY THAT MOVES. Splice two variable-length
672	  runs into one list and the split between them is not recorded, so
673	  moving an item from the first into the second leaves the SAME
674	  list and two different things wear one identity. `use a.b` and
675	  `use a.{b}` fingerprinted alike; so did `f<A>(B)` and
676	  `f<A, B?>()`, `f<B?>()` and `f(B)` (a written type and an ident
677	  were the same value), `fn f<T>(x: int)` and `fn f<T, x: int>()`.
678	  THE FIX IS ARITY: fold each sequence to ONE value so a payload's
679	  shape is fixed per kind. BOTH INTUITIVE FIXES ARE WRONG, and
680	  each is worth knowing. A SEPARATOR is the first —
681	  `stmt_fps(then).concat([0]).concat(stmt_fps(else))` was written by
682	  someone who saw this
683	  hazard exactly and spent the one value that is not spare, which
684	  is the empty-value law above wearing this law's clothes. A
685	  RENUMBERING is the second: under a LINEAR fold (`131t + x + 7`)
686	  a tag is an additive offset, so distinct tags separate nothing
687	  that a chosen literal can reach — renumbering turns the first
688	  test green and leaves every collision live. THE TEST: for each
689	  encoding ask which two shapes produce the same bytes, and write
690	  that pair as a test BEFORE the fix. Three collisions were
691	  nameable by hand here; enumerating every splice site and running
692	  it against the parent made nine.
693	  AND ITS QUIETER TWIN: A HASH THAT FORGETS A PAYLOAD. Same
694	  consequence — two values, one identity — but nothing to enumerate,
695	  because the omission leaves NO MARK at the site: the parts list
696	  reads complete. THE TEST IS A DIFF, the record's fields against the
697	  hash's parts, field by field. Seven were missing here in one sweep
698	  and every one was a field ADDED after its hash was written —
699	  `Param.mark` (so `fn f(mut x)` and `fn f(x)` were one statement),
700	  `Param.default`'s OWNER (a defaults list beside the fields says
701	  which exist, never whose), `TypeRef.dynamic`/`marks`/`arrow`,
702	  `export`, `StructSig.defaults`, and a named type whose whole
703	  signature hash was the constant `1`. So ask it of a hash on the
704	  same day a field lands, never of the hash alone.
705	  AND THE PART WORTH THE MOST: `export` was forgotten THREE LINES
706	  UNDER the comment that states the law — "A MARK IS PART OF THE
707	  STATEMENT: `fn f()`, `mut fn f()` and `once fn f()` declare
708	  different things". The doc named three of the five marks and the
709	  code stamped those three. A LAW WRITTEN AS A DOC COMMENT THAT
710	  ENUMERATES ITS INSTANCES DECAYS INTO A LIST, and the list stops
711	  growing before the code does; the reader sees a stated law and
712	  stops looking. `make fingerprints` is the enforcement now — it
713	  refuses a run spliced into a parts list (both surfaces witnessed
714	  failing), counts the lists it read, and claims the shared fold's
715	  tag in every file that CALLS it, since a borrowed tag mixes into
716	  that file's space.
717	- AN IDENTITY ASSIGNED LATE MUST RE-KEY WHAT WAS FILED UNDER ITS ABSENCE. The evaluator files the program's own run as
718	  a task the first time a task row asks (`rooted`), and a `contained` guard records the task that opened it — so a
719	  guard opened BEFORE any task row ran was filed under "no task" (-1), and the first `spawn`, wait or write inside
720	  its closure moved the run to task 0. The closure then returned to a guard that no longer matched, the guarded
721	  call's register took the closure's own answer (a `bool`) instead of the status 0, and the next compare read a
722	  bool where it wanted an int: "a non-int reached a runtime seat in a clean program", in the EVALUATOR only (native
723	  keeps no such table), and only when the closure's first task row was the program's first. It hid for as long as
724	  every guard's closure ran after the root was filed, and surfaced the first time a headless `turn` parsed JSON.
725	  THE TELL: a defect worded about a type, raised in a body nowhere near the type — the register was written by a
726	  path that mismatched silently (`guard_returned` answers null on a mismatch and the caller takes `gave`). THE FIX is
727	  in `rooted`, which re-keys the guards it finds; the witness is features/fns/tests/contained_rooted. Instrumenting
728	  the defect with the row, the body, the stack depth and the guard table found it in four builds: when a defect names
729	  a seat, print what wore it and who last wrote its register.
730	- A GUARD IS A PROPERTY OF EVERY CROSSING, NOT OF A PACKAGE. The law
731	  above says a NUL is spent at the C boundary; this one is where the
732	  refusal goes. THE CROSSING IS THE EXTERN SEAT, and only that: every
733	  verb in `@std/text` reads the header, so a NUL is an ordinary
734	  character on this side — text carrying one is longer than its
735	  prefix and unequal to it (`==`, `contains`, `index_of`, `split`,
736	  `replace` walk the length under `memcmp`/`memmem`, f57372a, and
737	  `starts_with` joined them here — it was left off that list and
738	  still walked with `strncmp`). It is
739	  `getenv`, `execvp`, `fopen`, `sqlite3_open` that end at the first
740	  NUL, so a value means a PREFIX of itself the moment it crosses, and
741	  the guard belongs at the row that hands the pointer over.
742	  `@std/text`'s `nul_at`/`has_nul` are that guard, once.
743	  THE SPREAD IS THE LESSON, and it is what made eight defects in two
744	  days across three packages: `@std/process` guarded `tool` and not
745	  `tool_from_env`; `@std/io` guarded ten verbs and not `env`;
746	  `@std/sqlite` guarded some and not five. Each package HAD the
747	  guard, one door down. The failures were SILENT, not traps — a holed
748	  name read a DIFFERENT variable (`env("PATH" + from_codepoint(0) +
749	  "/junk")` answered PATH's value), which no crash surfaces. SPELL
750	  THE EXAMPLE THE WAY THE HAZARD IS MINTED: this entry first wrote
751	  that name as `"PATH\0/junk"`, and `\0` IS NOT AN ESCAPE, so the
752	  demonstration contained no NUL and would have answered null for
753	  the wrong reason. @std/sqlite's boundary header taught the same
754	  trap with the same dead literal (fixed by the docs lead at
755	  e523655), in the file whose whole subject is that hazard. A doc
756	  that DEMONSTRATES a hazard is code that has never been run — the
757	  four guard cases here were witnessed failing with the guards
758	  removed, which is what a prose example cannot be. And A METHOD MUST NOT READ
759	  ONE NAME TWO WAYS: `Env.get` compared with `==` under `Only` and
760	  handed the name to C under `Inherit`, so one method disagreed with
761	  itself by variant. THE TEST: list every row that hands text to C,
762	  and diff it against the guarded ones — never "does this package
763	  guard".
764	  AND THE STALE-DOCTRINE TRAP THIS LAW WAS FIRST WRITTEN INTO. The
765	  first draft of this entry, and `@std/text`'s own module doc, and
766	  `std-sqlite/boundary.av`, all taught that those five verbs stop at
767	  a NUL. They DID until f57372a landed the same day, and I wrote the
768	  correction quoting the behavior the docs described instead of the
769	  behavior I measured — in the entry directly above the rule that
770	  says to measure. A doc is a claim with a date on it; the test that
771	  disagrees with it is the newer fact. `85abb9e`'s message carries
772	  the wrong rationale for a real fix because of it.
773	  AND A RETRACTED FACT SPREADS BY CITATION, WHICH NO SWEEP OF ITS
774	  ORIGIN REACHES. This one was quoted into four documents across
775	  three campaigns — a ROADMAP red-team entry, a docs vision's
776	  blockquote, a subset probe log's row, a census heading — and the
777	  package that OWNED the claim swept itself twice by file, correcting
778	  five sites, while every citation stood. A citation is a COPY that
779	  does not know it is one: it names the finding, not the mechanism,
780	  so it survives the mechanism changing and reads as corroboration
781	  from an independent source. THE SWEEP IS BY CLAIM, NEVER BY FILE
782	  OR BY PACKAGE — grep the tree for the ASSERTION and for the
783	  distinctive example that carries it (`ab\0cd`, `"\0x"` here), not
784	  for the files you remember writing.
785	- THE RUNTIME IS A LIBRARY AND THE HOST HOLDS EVERY ROW. A program
786	  links `build/libavra_runtime.a`, one object per `runtime/*.c`, and
787	  carries only what it reaches — so a program that never spawns carries
788	  no scheduler. The COMPILER must carry all of it, because its
789	  evaluator binds package C to the runtime inside its own process:
790	  `avra_rt.h`'s host table, generated from `rt_sigs()` and included by
791	  the extern host, names every row. A row with no evaluator arm is
792	  called by name through the uniform frame (`RtSig.armed`), so the
793	  frame's seat law holds for it — a closure cannot reach C that way.
794	- A FRAME NEVER SKIPS A GUARD. A task's stack has one guard page, and a
795	  frame wider than a page could step over it into a neighbour's stack.
796	  Every fn Avra emits carries `probe-stack`, and C built here probes
797	  too (Apple's clang by default, `-fstack-clash-protection`
798	  elsewhere). CHECK AN ATTACK BUILDS WHAT IT CLAIMS: the first
799	  wide-frame attack was a `volatile` array the compiler shrank to 16
800	  bytes, and it "passed".
801	- A COLD PATH IN A HOT LEAF COSTS EVERY CALL A FRAME. A lazy
802	  `getenv`, a `char msg[80]` for a trap's words, a grow branch, a
803	  `__builtin_return_address` read — each is free when it runs and
804	  ruinous where it sits, because the compiler hoists the register
805	  saves it needs ABOVE the fast path. `avra_rc_retain` saved four

# Avra — clean-room compiler

## AVRA PRINCIPLES

The spec's Part 0 frames every decision (full text: spec, Part 0).
Above all: **P6, paradox collapse** — binary choices are usually false
dichotomies; find the design where both sides win. When a trade-off
feels forced, the model is wrong, not the requirements.

- P1  LLM-first: correct on first generation is the success metric
- P2  substrate for autonomous services
- P3  gloriously declarative, zero ceremony
- P4  Rust-level performance or better
- P5  full-stack vertical integration
- P6  paradox collapse
- P7  visible magic — always inspectable
- P8  escape hatches everywhere
- P9  boundaries are contracts
- P10 the compiler holds semantic knowledge no other tool has
- P11 machine-readability is the substrate, human-readability the projection
- P12 one source of truth, many projections
- P13 collapse dev/ops/infra
- P14 no runtime, no framework, no container
- P17 composability over featurefulness

Clean restart of the Avra compiler, built slowly, one reviewed file at a
time. Front end first: an extensible grammar assembled from
LanguageFeature components, producing an AST for later passes.
Toolchain: the compiler builds itself — `./avra` runs `build/avra`,
and a cold tree bootstraps from `bootstrap/seed.ll.gz` (`make bootstrap`;
README.md).

Design sources of truth (in `../forge-crafting-intepreters`):
- `docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md` — the language
- `docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md` — node model, spans, error tolerance
- `bootstrap/docs/2026_08_19_STANDARDIZATION.md` — front-end shape

Follow the old tree's *documented designs*, never its code habits.

## Comments

Never write comments about specific situations, tickets, approaches, or
points in time. Comments are evergreen: always relevant, or absent.
Keep them very terse, in plain language. State what a thing is or the
invariant it holds — no narration, no self-justification, no history.

## The idiom bar — BEFORE writing any fn

First drafts are written idiomatic, not cleaned up later. Before
the body exists, answer:

1. Is any loop a MAP/FILTER/FLAT-MAP? Comprehension (`?` works in
   element and iterable; predicates hoist into named fns).
2. Building head-plus-tail? `concat` (a list METHOD) / `flatten`
   (core's FREE fn — `flatten(xs)`, never `xs.flatten()`), never
   push-ceremony.
3. Is a projection being spelled twice? The second spelling names a
   verb (`cx.int_at`, `expr_fps`) or uses the existing one.
4. Does absence read straight? (`?? `, `?.`, if-null early return —
   never a two-arm null match without payload logic on both arms.)
5. Scanning for one element? `find`/`any`/`index_of`, not a flag
   loop.
6. Unsure a shape compiles in the subset? PROBE in scratch first —
   fear of traps is how ugly-but-safe drafts happen, and every
   probe result gets recorded so the fear shrinks.

DOGFOODING.md is the full rulebook; `avra check --baseline
tools/idioms.baseline` FAILS on any NEW site — the baseline lists
sites, never counts, and no tool path can add to it (`make idioms`
runs every package, `make idioms-accept` prunes what a fix made
gone). Every idiom the language can state is a `rule` declaration,
found by `avra check` itself, and the gate counts a RULE's finding
only — `type.alias_copy` wears the same `warning[kind]` shape and is
the compiler's own law, never a rule, so the gate reads the rule
table (`avra rules --json`), never a kind-string shape. Accepted
debt lives in the baseline alone, reviewed at adoption and every
time after. A new idiom lands in DOGFOODING's registry AT DISCOVERY,
named by its rule — `<module>.<rule>`, never a number.

## Style

- Inline single-use values. A `let` earns its place only when the
  name carries meaning the expression lacks, the value is read more
  than once, or the subset REQUIRES a pin (a `dyn` value selected
  among arms, a Result-answering lambda — "The subset today" names
  each). Empty literals (`[]`, `{}`) infer inline in
  constructor fields — never bind them to a throwaway name. When a
  pin seems needed, probe before assuming.
- A state struct's impl is its VOCABULARY: the small verbs that
  read or write its tables (`speak`, `bind`, `mint`, `give`) live
  as methods, so drivers read as prose. The free state fns the
  bootstrap habit left (`eval_node(ev, cx, e)`, the interpreter's
  `put(m, …)`, the backend's `define(em, …)`) are methods now, and
  so are the pass contexts' whole vocabularies (`cx.accepts(e,
  want)`, `cx.open_region(c)`, `ws.sig(d)` — 320 verbs, one sweep);
  style.free_state_verb refuses a new free verb in the pass's own files. A PASS ENTRY
  POINT (`lower(a: Analysis)`, `memory(l: Lowered)`) keeps the one
  standard signature and is not a verb.
- A long fn splits at its PHASE boundaries into named helpers, each
  with a one-line contract (`match_seq` matches, `built` builds —
  grammar/executor.av; `window` frames, `severity_word` branches —
  diagnostics/render.av). If a fn needs a paragraph comment
  mid-body, that paragraph is a helper's name.
- A LAW never assembles PROSE: every refusal is a NAMED VOICE fn
  (its whole body the one `spoken`/`emit`), in a voices section at
  the file's tail or shared where features share words. Rule
  bodies read as guard + verb (rule.compiler.refusal_assembled;
  enums/check.av is the exemplar).
  AND A VOICE STATES THE LAW, NOT THE SYMPTOM. "a pointer's only
  constant is null" is the rule; "both engines read it as null" was
  the observation that happened to hold the day it was written. A
  symptom-worded refusal goes STALE the moment the mechanism moves,
  and until then it reads as a workaround for a quirk rather than a
  rule to obey — so it teaches the reader to look for the quirk. The
  law's wording outlives its own implementation, which is what makes
  it worth pinning in the golden (lower.av's pointer-constant guard).
- A BUILDER'S WORDS ARE ITS CLAIM. A builder's refusal is carried
  WHOLE into its diagnostic (grammar/executor.av's build phase:
  `cause: Cause.Builder, message: m`), so a message that is a LAW
  the writer broke reads as the law, and one that is a DEFECT says
  so in its own words. A blanket "builder failed:" prefix once told
  the reader the compiler had broken about every law — five of the
  seven refusals sampled at c7b5038 — while `Cause` had separated
  `Builder` from `Defect` all along: the seam was right and only the
  WORDING lied. THE GENERAL SHAPE: A PARAPHRASE OF A FLAG IS A
  SECOND COPY, and the reader believes the words — the flag is
  checked by the code, the prose by nobody. So the WORDS carry the
  CLAIM and the STRUCTURE carries the CATEGORY (`Cause.Builder`
  projects to F0102, compiler/codes.av), and the words never restate
  the category.
- A projection is ONE match: nested patterns
  (`.Node(.NAlt(a)) -> a, _ -> null`), never an unwrap ladder.
- The third copy of a shape names the concept: shared walks and
  registries get ONE definition (`post_order`, `file_command`) and
  the copies die. Two copies may wait; three never do.

## Dogfooding is design

The compiler is Avra's first user. When its code WANTS a construct
the language lacks — a sugar, a projection, a rule — add the ask to
the ROADMAP's sugar backlog, naming the wanting site, as part of the
change that hit it. Request your own features: the backlog feeds the
spec. The same discipline runs one level down: a PATTERN discovered
while writing (a beautiful form, a smell, a licensed exception) is
an IDIOM — it lands in DOGFOODING.md's registry at discovery, and
the greppable ones become `rule` declarations `avra check` finds
directly (compiler/idioms.av, or a feature's own idioms.av). The
registry is the idiom engine's spec, written by dogfooding.

## Rules

- `core/` is infrastructure only. Features never import features.
- Layering is one-way: core -> grammar -> features -> compiler, all
  over `@std/relation`, whose `engine/` is the memo kernel —
  infrastructure, language-agnostic, the one a running program asks too.
  `grammar/` is the language-agnostic engine; `compiler/` is the
  driver and the ONE definition of Avra (feature order is branch
  order is the language).
- No string tags or string-matching to detect behavior.
- `_ ->` over our own enums is decided by COUNTING THE ANSWERING
  ARMS. One arm answers -> a PROJECTION, and the catch-all is
  honest: its contract pins the answer for variants that do not
  exist yet. TWO OR MORE answer -> a REGISTRY, and a catch-all there
  silently forgets the next variant (`let_name` dropped For's
  counter exactly so; `type_decl_name` would have swallowed the next
  type-declaring statement). Registries spell every arm — `or`-runs
  keep that affordable. Ratcheted as style.registry_catchall AND held by the compiler:
  F2040 counts the ANSWERING ARMS over the declared enum and names
  the variants a hole would forget. The license is a SPELLING, not a
  comment — `rest ->` says the remainder is deliberate, and both the
  compiler and the ratchet read it. The two licensed shapes are a
  feature matching its own variants (it cannot enumerate other
  features') and a loop that DELEGATES the rest to an exhaustive
  dispatch — each writes `rest ->` at the site.
  AND THE LAW IS ABOUT THE TEST, NOT THE MATCH. For a REGISTRY enum
  `is .Variant` IS A CATCH-ALL IN DIFFERENT CLOTHES: a boolean that
  asks about ONE variant and falls through for the rest discharges
  the registry's obligation no better than `_ ->`, and it is harder
  to see. For a PROJECTION enum it stays the right idiom. Two
  `RtKind` consumers were written that way (`rt_arg`, `answers_word`
  in llvm.av), correct only while the enum had three variants —
  widening it to carry C's integer widths would have sent an Avra
  `int` into an `i32` seat with no truncation, compiling clean. Both
  are exhaustive matches now.
  ENFORCEMENT SPLITS FROM THE LAW HERE, deliberately: no grep tells a
  registry enum from a projection one, so this gets NO ratchet rule.
  The keeper is `make vocab`, a CURATED table naming each registry's
  consumers and refusing BOTH shapes inside them — the table says
  which registries it holds, and a registry it does not name is
  unguarded. Naming the next one IS how this law is enforced.
  AND THE OBLIGATION CROSSES INTO C, where no keeper can follow. The
  runtime's `acc_kind_of` was a kind-keyed ternary falling through to
  ACC_RECORD — correct for the three kinds that existed when it was
  written and wrong from that same day for `KIND_STATIC`, so every
  immortal string was filed as a RECORD by `AVRA_MEM_STATS`: the
  instrument THIS FILE names as the way to answer a memory question,
  miscounting its own data since birth. A C chain keyed on our kinds
  carries a registry's obligation and `make vocab` cannot see it, so
  spell the kinds there too.
  AND THE REASON IT HID GENERALIZES: `RtKind` had three variants from
  the day it was written and had not yet grown — it carries six now
  — so nothing ever tested the assumption. A KEEPER THAT HAS ONLY
  EVER GUARDED A STATIC ENUM IS UNTESTED — the first widening is its
  first real test, and that is the worst moment to learn it was only
  ever looking for one shape.
  AND THE OBLIGATION CROSSES A PACKAGE BOUNDARY TOO, not only into C.
  A registry keyed on ANOTHER PACKAGE'S enum is spelled over NAMES —
  `node_value` matches `@std.meta.Node`'s variant names, because a
  foreign enum has no typed id here — so no compiler law and no grep
  sees it, and its `_ -> null` forgot the next variant the way every
  registry hole does: a template generated nothing and nobody was
  told. The keeper cannot follow across the seam; spell the arms and
  make the unknown SPEAK.
- THE EXEMPTION LAW, which the above is one instance of: a doctrine
  exemption that is not written AT THE SITE is an unbounded amnesty.
  Prose exemptions are invisible to tooling and to the next reader,
  so they rot into the default. Every licensed deviation carries
  `// LICENSED I<n>: <reason>` where the code is — that is what
  makes `make idioms` able to demand a decision instead of guessing
  which deviations were once approved.
- Node facts (spans included) live in side tables keyed by typed ids,
  never on nodes.
- A SLOT'S SEED IS COMPUTED THE SAME WAY AS ITS UPDATES, or the
  first decision judges a different quantity from every later one —
  and only the first, which is what makes it invisible.
  `collapse_breaks` seeded `line_indent` from `raw[0].span.lo`, a
  byte OFFSET, and assigned it a character DISTANCE everywhere after;
  the seed read as a column only while the first token sat on line
  one, so a LEADING COMMENT's own length became the indent and a
  four-character comment changed how the file parsed. Write the seed
  as the update's rule applied to nothing, not as whatever value
  happens to be at hand.
- A fact EVERY BODY MAY READ is answered from the PROGRAM — the
  store — never from a pass's fact tables. Fact tables are per
  declaration, over that declaration's expression range alone, so an
  answer computed from `facts` is right in the body that recorded it
  and WRONG everywhere else (a const's declared `int?` read back as
  `int` across a fn floor, and `??` warned it would never fire).
  The store holds what the program wrote; that is what shared
  answers are made of.
- A law that HOLDS A BINDING TO ITS ANNOTATION compares the value to
  the DECLARED type it computed, never to the binding's own type —
  asking the binding for its type compares the value against itself,
  and the law silently stops refusing anything.
- Ask a BINDING, never a NAME, whether it is a const/a capture/a
  seat. A name may be defined twice (a `let` shadowing a const), so
  a name-keyed question and the binding in hand answer about
  DIFFERENT statements — the mismatch reads a slot nobody wrote
  ("index -1"). One question, asked of the statement. And a
  name-keyed table holds what it holds: `resolve_assign` asked
  `binding_of(name)`, a LOCALS table, so a fn's name walked
  through as a place — the walk had already recorded the root's
  binding; ask that.
- A BODY IS TYPED UNDER ITS SIGNATURE, so a declaration whose
  SIGNATURE WAS REFUSED has no scope for its body to be typed in —
  and the empty list that stands in for the missing one is read as
  a real scope by every seat. `walk_under` sets `self.scope =
  sig?.params ?? []`, the plausible default the protocol law
  refuses, and `target_type`'s `.Param(i) -> self.scope[i]` then
  indexed past the end: a generic METHOD is refused whole (F2031,
  no sig recorded) and its body still walks, so `fn f<T: Tr>(x: T)
  { x.m() }` inside an `impl` CRASHED THE COMPILER while the same
  fn at the top level was fine. The tell was a SIBLING PAIR
  disagreeing in one match — `.Receiver -> self.scope.first() ??
  self.error_type` was total and `.Param(i)` was not, four lines
  apart, so one seat kind had the guard and the other did not.
  SEVERAL SPELLINGS OF ONE QUESTION IS THE DEFECT, not the missing
  bound: every one asks "what type does seat i wear", and one file
  held five — two receiver reads, total, and three parameter reads,
  none of them. The split was invisible because each pair sat
  inside ONE match, arms apart, so a reader checking either arm saw
  a guard right beside it. There is one reader now (`seat_type`),
  and the refusal was already spoken before the body ran, which is
  what makes Error the honest answer rather than a defect voice.
- A COPIED TEMPLATE'S SPANS ARE ITS ORIGIN FILE'S OFFSETS — so its
  errors point home — and any pass that reads a span as THIS file's
  offset must ask `store.spanned_elsewhere(e)` first. `range_bodies`
  did not, and `within`'s copied nodes landed in whatever `client.av`
  declared at `time.av`'s offsets (a write through `self` blamed on
  `describe`). A sublanguage's nodes are foreign too but spanned HERE
  (shifted into the block); `ForeignRange.spanned_home` tells them apart.
- A READ WEARS THE TYPE OF WHAT IS READ, never the type of the node
  doing the reading. This bit THREE times in one slice: a captured
  callee took the CALL's type (a call's type is its answer, never its
  callee's), a capture took the LAMBDA's type (a lambda is a managed
  box, so an `int` capture looked managed and the memory pass
  retained a number), and a field read took the field expression's
  type where the SUBJECT's decides the layout. A register's recorded
  type is the wrong witness under mono, where it may still name a
  type parameter; the STATIC type of the thing being read is right.
- UNIFY BINDS, `accepts` RECORDS. `unify` agrees two types and pins a
  declaration's Vars; it does NOT record the lift that lowering
  mints. A seat that unifies and returns without passing through the
  agreement door silently drops the widen — invisible for as long as
  the widen happens to be identity, and a wrong answer the day the
  representation changes. The door is ONE verb, `agreed` (checks.av),
  and the three unified seats — a call argument, a struct field, an

  direction — a seat that PERMITS writing accepts a callee that does

  believes is spare, and the spare value is almost always the empty

  the premise that hides is "nothing is not a real value here", and
  it hides inside code that is sound everywhere else. Three

  nameable by hand here; enumerating every splice site and running
  it against the parent made nine.

## AVRA PRINCIPLES

Above all: **P6, paradox collapse** — binary choices are usually false
dichotomies; find the design where both sides win. When a trade-off
feels forced, the model is wrong, not the requirements.

- P1  LLM-first: correct on first generation is the success metric
- P2  substrate for autonomous services
- P3  gloriously declarative, zero ceremony
- P4  Rust-level performance or better
- P5  full-stack vertical integration
- P6  paradox collapse
- P7  visible magic — always inspectable
- P8  escape hatches everywhere
- P9  boundaries are contracts
- P10 the compiler holds semantic knowledge no other tool has
- P11 machine-readability is the substrate, human-readability the projection
- P12 one source of truth, many projections
- P13 collapse dev/ops/infra
- P14 no runtime, no framework, no container
- P17 composability over featurefulness

Clean restart of the Avra compiler, built slowly, one reviewed file at a
time. Front end first: an extensible grammar assembled from
LanguageFeature components, producing an AST for later passes.
Toolchain: the compiler builds itself — `./avra` runs `build/avra`,
and a cold tree bootstraps from `bootstrap/seed.ll.gz` (`make bootstrap`;
README.md).

Design sources of truth (in `../forge-crafting-intepreters`):
- `docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md` — the language
- `docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md` — node model, spans, error tolerance
- `bootstrap/docs/2026_08_19_STANDARDIZATION.md` — front-end shape

Follow the old tree's *documented designs*, never its code habits.

## Comments

Never write comments about specific situations, tickets, approaches, or
points in time. Comments are evergreen: always relevant, or absent.
Keep them very terse, in plain language. State what a thing is or the
invariant it holds — no narration, no self-justification, no history.

   push-ceremony.

   verb (`cx.int_at`, `expr_fps`) or uses the existing one.

   never a two-arm null match without payload logic on both arms.)

   loop.

   fear of traps is how ugly-but-safe drafts happen, and every
   probe result gets recorded so the fear shrinks.

tools/idioms.baseline` FAILS on any NEW site — the baseline lists
sites, never counts, and no tool path can add to it (`make idioms`

named by its rule — `<module>.<rule>`, never a number.
